about: The kanji a `_ruby` twin may use (rule R1 in review/judge_ruby.json): the Tanos JLPT N5 and N4 kanji lists. A word with any other kanji is written in hiragana. One field prints kanji itself (Mari's sign 「立入禁止」 in mari.L33.3), so its twin keeps the printed kanji. test_kanji_list.py checks every twin against this file, and this file against the archived Tanos pages in pipeline/jp/tanos/.
retrieved_via: www.tanos.co.uk did not resolve on 2026-10-26. The Tanos pages themselves were read that day from the Internet Archive (primary_snapshots below, each page marked 'Updated: November 21, 2010') and are committed byte for byte under pipeline/jp/tanos/. Each level's string here is that page's kanji table, one row per kanji, in the page's order. The lists were first taken from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidluzgouveia/kanji-data/00fd7079c3890f430759536f91aa5e854ec0ca4f/kanji.json, field jlpt_new (5 and 4), whose README credits the Tanos JLPT Resources page for its JLPT levels; the archived pages hold the same two sets, kanji for kanji.
cross_check: Neither Tanos page states a count in prose: the count is the rows of its kanji table, 79 on the N5 page and 166 on the N4 page, and neither page holds 分. The phase 3 ask text named 80 N5 kanji; that figure was the ask's, not the page's. Another copy of the Tanos lists, https://github.com/Bluskyo/JLPT_Vocabulary at 4358f932937ad0232194a36e9f4f875094910c6b (data/kanji/parsedData/n5_kanji.csv and n4_kanji.csv, parsed from the Tanos PDFs), holds the same two sets, kanji for kanji. jisho.org, whose JLPT data comes from the Tanos page, reported the same counts on 2026-10-26: 'Kanji — 79 found' for #kanji #jlpt-n5 and 'Kanji — 166 found' for #kanji #jlpt-n4.
N5: 日一国人年大十二本中長出三時行見月後前生五間上東四今金九入学高円子外八六下来気小七山話女北午百書先名川千水半男西電校語土木聞食車何南万毎白天母火右読友左休父雨
N4: 会同事自社発者地業方新場員立開手力問代明動京目通言理体田主題意不作用度強公持野以思家世多正安院心界教文元重近考画海売知道集別物使品計死特私始朝運終台広住真有口少町料工建空急止送切転研足究楽起着店病質待試族銀早映親験英医仕去味写字答夜音注帰古歌買悪図週室歩風紙黒花春赤青館屋色走秋夏習駅洋旅服夕借曜飲肉貸堂鳥飯勉冬昼茶弟牛魚兄犬妹姉漢
operator_note: Ruling of 2026-10-26: the pronoun わたし is written 私{わたし}. 私 is in the N4 list, so it needs no addition. 分 (わかる) is on neither Tanos page, so under the strict ruling わかる is written in hiragana; it joins the twins only as a recorded operator addition.
